title: 3DSS: 3D Surface Splatting for Inverse Rendering
description:
arXiv:2605.05876v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We present 3D Surface Splatting (3DSS), the first differentiable surface splatting renderer for physically-based inverse rendering from multi-view images. Our central insight is that surface separation, which groups the surfels covering a pixel by the surface they sample, can be formulated with the reconstruction kernels themselves: two surfels sample the same surface when their kernels overlap in depth. Compositing each resulting surface layer with a coverage opacity derived from its accumulated Elliptical Weighted Average (EWA) weight yields anti-aliased silhouettes and informative visibility gradients at sparsely covered edges. With forward microfacet shading under co-optimized HDR environment lighting, 3DSS jointly recovers shape, spatially-varying BRDF, and illumination, and its oriented surfels convert directly into meshes by oriented-point surface reconstruction. On the real-world Stanford-ORB and the TensoIR Synthetic benchmarks, 3DSS outperforms state-of-the-art mesh-based and major comparable implicit and Gaussian-based methods in novel view synthesis and relighting, with geometry on par with the strongest baselines.
